Timeline::gt¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::gt(const Timeline& other) const
Series Timeline::operator>(const Timeline& other) const

Instants After A Boundary¶

gt() reports where the left instant occurs strictly after the right instant. It is the strict lower-bound relation.

const auto times = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-01T02:00:00Z"});
const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
std::cout << pluss::series::print(times > start) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[false, true]

Equality at the first position is excluded. Use ge() to include it.

Pairwise And Broadcasted Questions¶

A scalar boundary is only the simplest case. Two equally shaped Timelines are compared position by position, and lower-rank operands broadcast across compatible trailing dimensions. The operation never searches for “the next” instant; it only compares the pairs established by broadcasting.

NaT is unordered, so either operand being absent produces false. Use isnat() alongside gt() if absence must be represented as a separate state.

Non-broadcastable shapes throw before a mask is returned.
